PullRequest.Title: Add sandbox policy reports to Copilot agent sessions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42182471-09a8-46b9-b2e5-a9480c932864

Add `/sandbox-policy` to Copilot agent-host sessions. The VS Code command invokes the SDK's existing `/sandbox policy` command and presents its effective policy as a persisted Markdown report, without starting a model turn or changing sandbox enforcement.

## User experience

- Offer `/sandbox-policy` in slash-command completion while keeping native `/sandbox` subcommands hidden.
- Show an **Open Sandbox Policy** link in the response that opens the formatted report in Markdown preview.
- Use normal theme-aware chat link colors, including hover and active states.
- Support mouse, Enter, and Space activation, with accessible-help guidance.
- Save a unique report for each invocation so earlier links continue to show their original snapshots.

## Implementation

- Introduce optional host-side `getInvocation` and `getOutput` hooks on resolved slash commands, separate from SDK catalog metadata. Omitted hooks or hooks returning `undefined` preserve the existing SDK invocation and output behavior.
- Support structured text and link output with optional Markdown and preview flags. Keep command lifecycle, mode handling, and runtime-settings invalidation in the session.
- Keep sandbox-specific argument validation, SDK mapping, policy formatting, and report persistence in `CopilotSandboxPolicyDisplay`.
- Strip ANSI styling, preserve SDK Markdown, format recognized terminal policy reports, and safely fence unrecognized plain text. Propagate invocation and file-write failures instead of emitting broken links.
- Preserve preview metadata across local and remote Agent Host URI rewriting without passing it to filesystem providers.
- Extract a reusable single-anchor rendering helper to avoid a second anchor scan. Repeated decoration does not register duplicate widgets or listeners.
- Reuse the shared SDK command type in completion handling.

## Compatibility

- Existing commands retain their default invocation and rendering when no custom behavior applies.
- Preserve native sandbox aliases and raw SDK input; do not format unrelated sandbox subcommands or client commands as policy reports.
- Reserve the host alias against runtime name collisions and keep it discoverable when SDK command discovery fails.
- No SDK dependency changes, new permissions, or sandbox-policy enforcement changes.

## Validation

- **803 targeted tests passed** across Copilot session, command-handler, completion, Markdown rendering, inline-anchor, URI adapter, and accessibility-help suites.
- Regression coverage includes local/remote preview links, rich links enabled/disabled, keyboard activation, report formatting and persistence, error propagation, optional-hook fallbacks, and duplicate-widget prevention.
- A 1,001-link regression test verifies a single anchor scan with 1,000 ordinary links and one preview link.
- Core typecheck and transpile watchers completed with zero errors.
- ESLint passed for changed refactor files; CSS lint passed with only pre-existing design-token suggestions.
- Dark and light Component Explorer fixtures render without errors; preview-link colors were checked against regular chat links.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke /sandbox-policy or /sandbox policy in a Copilot agent-host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Mode application completes first, then one SDK commands.invoke RPC returns the policy, formatting runs in-process, and one session-data file write completes before the response link is emitted. All work is on the command response critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the SDK sandbox policy command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one commands.invoke RPC per explicit policy command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native /sandbox policy already invoked the SDK once; the new /sandbox-policy alias maps to that same existing SDK operation rather than adding per-item calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the policy response until the SDK returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the formatted policy as sandbox-policy.md
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one write per successful policy invocation, with one unique snapshot retained per invocation until session deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native sandbox policy output was rendered inline and performed no report-file write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The link is emitted only after the write succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation produces one policy payload and one unique Markdown snapshot; cost grows linearly with explicit user invocations and policy text size, not with conversation turns or workspace files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The mode RPC, command invocation, formatting, and file write are awaited sequentially. Concurrent user turns remain governed by the existing session lifecycle; this diff adds no fan-out or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The host alias resolves without SDK catalog discovery. Native /sandbox uses the existing coalesced slash-command catalog cache. Reports intentionally use unique paths, so there is no overwrite cache; the containing per-session directory is deleted on session removal and startup orphan cleanup handles abandoned sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the sequential one-RPC/one-write path and session-level cleanup based on direct call flow and SessionDataService deletion behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK policy payload sizes and user invocation frequency are not measured, but the trigger is explicit and expected policy output is small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new I/O is the requested persisted-report behavior, is one operation per explicit invocation, has no collection fan-out, and is bounded by session-data cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and open the sandbox-policy Markdown preview link in chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Markdown parsing and URI rewriting run during response rendering, followed by one DOM anchor scan. The preview link creates one inline-anchor widget; its file stat is asynchronous and does not block initial rendering. Opening the link later performs the normal opener/editor filesystem read on the user gesture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the preview report resource while constructing its inline anchor widget
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous stat for the single policy preview link per rendered DOM instance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The policy preview link and its widget did not exist, so no corresponding stat occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after widget construction and does not block the initial rendered response; it only refines file/folder icon state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/read the Markdown report through the opener and preview editor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open operation per user click or keyboard activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no persisted policy report to open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only affects the explicit open-report action, not chat response rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Decoration CPU scales with anchors in the rendered Markdown and with streaming re-renders. The policy response has one preview anchor; ordinary anchors are not converted to widgets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous anchor loop runs per Markdown render. Each preview widget starts one asynchronous stat; the policy output contributes a single stat and no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is involved in decoration. Already-rendered anchors are recognized to prevent duplicate widgets/listeners within the same DOM. Normal chat re-render disposal recreates widgets consistently with existing content-part lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that there is one anchor scan and one widget/stat for the policy response, supported by the changed loop, duplicate guard, and test coverage.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large generated Markdown responses can contain many query-bearing links and may be re-rendered while streaming, but the added URI parsing is lightweight relative to existing Markdown/DOM reconstruction and the reviewed policy path emits one completed link.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff avoids a second anchor scan, does not register duplicate widgets, and the only new filesystem work is one asynchronous stat plus a user-triggered open for the requested report.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request slash-command completions while typing in a Copilot agent-host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Completion requests consult the slash-command provider. A cold catalog lookup awaits the existing SDK commands.list RPC subject to its existing timeout; warm requests use the cached catalog, then prepend the host command and filter a name collision in memory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced RPC per cold cache generation, not per command or completion item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached and coalesced commands.list RPC populated slash completions before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold completion can wait for the existing bounded lookup; warm completion has no boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU/allocation scales with the small runtime command catalog on each completion request; effective catalog cardinality is deduplicated by the existing cache builder.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold command-list requests are coalesced by the existing inFlight promise. The diff introduces no additional RPC or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold lookup performs the existing SDK list call; warm lookups reuse cache.value. Cache invalidation behavior is unchanged. If discovery fails, only the static host alias is returned.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the provider cache and inFlight coalescing implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalog sizes and keystroke frequency vary, but catalogs are expected to remain small and no boundary cardinality changed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only added work is a small in-memory filter/array construction over the cached catalog; expensive discovery frequency is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rewrite Agent Host file links for local or remote chat rendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each internal, non-external link is parsed and mapped to an Agent Host URI during Markdown rendering. The diff additionally extracts and restores presentation metadata using URLSearchParams; no I/O occurs in this function.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU and temporary allocation scale linearly with internal links and render count; external links return before the new query parsing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per-link transformation with no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network activity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or invalidated. The transformation is deterministic and preserves ordinary resource query parameters.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the change is in-process URL parsing only and does not add a boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Responses with unusually many internal links could amplify parsing allocation, but no evidence shows a user-visible regression beyond the already linear per-link URI transformation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added metadata manipulation is linear, bounded by rendered links, and does not alter boundary-call cardinality or move I/O onto the render path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run agent-host file-operation E2E suites on Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test registration evaluates a platform/provider gate; when disabled, the affected replay test is not executed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One boolean decision for one test case.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changed product concurrency; this is test-only configuration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because all changed files in this scenario are test harness, provider test configuration, or documentation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None relevant to shipped product performance.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance impact and no reportable issue.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 24 changed files and all diff pages. Traced command invocation, SDK catalog caching/coalescing, policy formatting and persistence, session-data cleanup, Agent Host URI rewriting, Markdown decoration, widget lifecycle, asynchronous file stats, report opening, and test-only changes. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
